# v1.1.0-dev.80 — The app has an icon of its own

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.79`.

One change, and it's the one you see before you open anything.

## An Icon, Instead Of Electron's Default

Every build so far shipped with the stock Electron icon on the
executable. That's what showed up in the taskbar, in Explorer, in
Alt+Tab, and on any shortcut you made. Nothing about it said WLM.

There's a real one now. Three panes, one tall one beside two stacked,
in the same cyan the rest of the app uses. It's the shape the visual
editor draws and the shape the `▦` in the title bar has been standing
in for. The colours come straight out of the app's stylesheet, which
is what makes the icon and the window read as the same thing.

The tray icon changed with it. The old one was a four-square grid
close enough to the Windows logo to be worth not having, sitting in a
notification area that already has one of those.

### Every Size Is Drawn, Not Shrunk

An icon isn't one picture. Windows asks for a different one depending
on where it's putting it. The usual shortcut is to draw a big one and
let the shell squash it down, which is what makes small icons look
soft.

Each size gets rendered from the vector on its own instead. The whole
mark sits on a grid that divides evenly at 16 pixels, putting every
edge on a whole pixel rather than straddling two. The little title
strips along the top of each pane only appear at 48 pixels and up,
because below that they're smaller than a pixel and all they do is
muddy the edges.

Ten sizes ship in the executable: 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 96, 128
and 256. The middle ones aren't padding. Windows scales the *logical*
size at 125% and 150% display scaling, so a taskbar on a scaled
monitor is asking for 20 and 24 rather than reaching for 16 and
stretching it.

### The Tray Wanted A Different Format Entirely

Windows reads an `.ico` and picks the frame it wants out of it. The
notification area doesn't work that way through Electron: the tray is
handed a finished bitmap, and an `.ico` gets collapsed to a single
256-pixel image on the way there. That meant a 48-pixel drawing blown
up to 256 and then squeezed back down to 16 by the shell, which looks
exactly as bad as it sounds.

So the tray gets a separate set of PNGs, one per display scaling.
Electron hands over the exact bitmap for whichever monitor the taskbar
is on. Its greys also sit further toward the middle than the app
icon's, because with no tile behind it the mark lands straight on a
taskbar that might be nearly black or nearly white.

### It Can't Go Stale Quietly

The icons are generated and committed rather than built on the fly. If
a regeneration never ran, the old files would sit there and nothing
would complain. `npm test` now parses the committed icons the way the
shell does and fails on a missing size, a truncated file, an icon that
decodes to nothing, or any of the code paths drifting off the asset
paths.

Regenerating them is `npm run icons`. Chromium does the drawing, which
keeps the no-native-build rule intact and adds no image library to
install.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
